New month, new sawdust.

Yesterday, MSc Biomedical Engineering (MDI) Cohort 2 kicked off October with their first  woodworking class. First cuts, first joints, first feel of building something with their own hands.

Here is to a month of building.

Kenyatta University Rice University The Lemelson Foundation MedTech Kenyatta University Eubrea Mitchy Anthonius Waka
#InventionEducationKU #MedTechAfrica #KenyattaUniversity #MDI #Woodworking #Prototyping

Today at CDIE, a group of innovators gathered for a hands-on 3D printing workshop, moving from digital design to physical prototype. Students, interns, and builders at different stages of their journeys came to learn the craft of turning a concept into something you can hold, test, and improve.

With the right tools and the talent, together we will bring Ideas to objects one layer at a time. 

Kenyatta University Rice University The Lemelson Foundation MedTech Kenyatta University
#InventionEducationKU #MedTechAfrica #KenyattaUniversity #3DPrinting #Prototyping #CDIE

On the evening of 19th August, Antler space in Nairobi filled with women rewriting what healthcare can look like in Africa.

As part of the MedTech Connect Series, and in partnership with Medevice, Invention Education Kenyatta University hosted:  ‘Women in STEM: Transforming Healthcare’.

It brought together an extraordinary cross-section of the ecosystem. Biomedical engineers from Mama Lucy Kibaki, Machakos Level 5, Mbagathi, and Kiambu hospitals. Founders and CEOs building companies like Waridi Labs, Hakikisho Labs, and EBikes Africa. Doctors, lecturers, technical engineers, and students from Kenyatta University, the Technical University of Mombasa, and beyond.

What connected them was not a job title. It was a shared conviction that science, technology, engineering, and innovation are how we close the gaps in African healthcare, and that women belong at the centre of that work.

To every woman who showed up, spoke up, and connected: thank you for reminding us what the future of healthcare looks like.
Kenyatta University Rice University The Lemelson Foundation MedTech Kenyatta University
#InventionEducationKU #MedTechAfrica #KenyattaUniversity #WomenInSTEM #WomenInHealthcare #MedTechConnect

Meet our champions. 🏆

The IvE Design Challenge: Maternal & Neonatal Care has its winners.
🥇  KACare. Team Members : Khalil Awadh & Andrew Abila
🥈 KMC-VEST. Team Members: Kiprotich Mololu, @Martin Magu, Munene Mwaniki, Ishmael Njoka, Austin Muchiri
 
Both teams now advance to represent CDIE at the continental NEST360 challenge, competing for a $2,000 prize and a platform to scale their work.

Tomorrow, a week of work meets the stage. 🏆

The IvE Design Challenge: Maternal & Neonatal Care reaches its final day tomorrow at CDIE, Kenyatta University.

Eight teams from across universities have spent the week turning  maternal and newborn health needs into working solutions: KMC Vest, Pawanax, MaternalGuard, KACare, DINRA, Obs-ervers, NeoBridge, and NERSZ.

Tomorrow they pitch. The judges deliberate. Two teams earn the right to represent CDIE at the continental NEST360 challenge.
